title: The Evolution of Human Consciousness and AI are the Two Divergent Pathways to Non-Hierarchical Coordination Beyond Team-Scale
content: As a form of theory elaboration, a comparative case illustration of two extremely divergent cases is employed to explore the two radically different evolutionary pathways that could challenge the well-documented team-scale barrier to non-hierarchical coordination. The first pathway is via Frederic Laloux’s proposed “evolution of human consciousness” combined with Mary Parker Follett’s “invisible leader”, and the second pathway is via the evolution of AI. The first case illustration explores a potentially unique example of scalable coordination via elevated human consciousness. A proposed pre-industrial anomaly is analyzed in the organization capability of the Apaches. Based on a distinctive nantan/diyin co-leadership relationship, non-hierarchical strategic coordination may have exceeded the team-scale barrier, despite the bounded rationality constraints that would normally apply. Moreover, their resilience endured across centuries of extreme environmental pressure and genocidal onslaught. This was in stark contrast to the Aztecs, Incas, and Indigenous contemporaries, whose political and military power backed by larger civilizations collapsed almost immediately once the European conquerors arrived. Arguably, the Apaches may have had one of the most resilient and scalable decentralized organizations in human history. However, despite their extraordinary resilience, the pre-industrial conditions that facilitated the proposed Apache model may be an anachronistic anomaly beyond our reach to replicate. As a result, a viable pathway towards organization-scale strategic coordination may require some form of AI. Even more so at modern societal-scale levels, it is argued that AI coevolution will likely be indispensable in achieving increasingly multidimensional human coordination. The business ecosystem platform of the Chinese company Haier is analyzed as the second case illustration to elucidate humanity’s most recent stage of societal-scale coordination via AI. Although this second case points to a viable pathway towards more complex evolutionary levels of multidimensional coordination, AI has still not succeeded in breaking the team-scale barrier without hierarchical coordination.
